title: Sets: a survey of sport in a class
source:
Forty students in a Form 4 class were asked which of two sports they play.

25 students play football (F).
20 students play cricket (C).
8 students play both football and cricket.

Every student in the class answered the question.
prompt: Answer ALL parts of the question. (This question is the Sets question of Section I and carries 5 marks.)

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Draw a Venn diagram to show this information, writing in the number of students in each region.
parts.modelAnswer: Draw two overlapping circles labelled F and C inside a rectangle for the class. The overlap holds 8 (both sports). Football only = 25 - 8 = 17. Cricket only = 20 - 8 = 12. Outside the circles, inside the rectangle, write 3 for the students who play neither sport.
markScheme: 1 mark for two correctly labelled overlapping sets with 8 in the intersection.
1 mark for 17 in F only, 12 in C only and 3 outside the circles.
No marks for an unlabelled diagram or for regions that do not add up to 40.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the number of students in the class who play neither sport.
parts.modelAnswer: n(F U C) = 17 + 8 + 12 = 37. Students who play neither = 40 - 37 = 3.
markScheme: 1 mark for n(F U C) = 37 (or for adding the regions correctly).
1 mark for 40 - 37 = 3.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Describe, in words, the set F ' (F complement) in this context, and state how many students it contains.
parts.modelAnswer: F ' is the set of students who do NOT play football. It contains the 12 cricket-only students and the 3 students who play neither sport, that is 15 students in all.
markScheme: 1 mark for a correct description (students who do not play football) with the cardinality 15.

planningHints: Start with the overlap, then take it away from each total.
Check the four regions add to 40.
examinerTips: Diagrams must be pencil-sharp and labelled; examiners cannot award a mark for a region they cannot identify.

title: Consumer arithmetic: discounts, hire purchase and commission
source:
A furniture and appliance store advertises a refrigerator with a marked price of $4,800.00.

The store offers two ways of buying it:

  Cash: a discount of 15% off the marked price.
  Hire purchase: a deposit of 20% of the marked price and 12 monthly instalments of $372.00.

The store also advertises a savings plan paying 6% per annum compound interest, and its sales staff earn a basic wage of $2,400.00 a month plus a commission of 2% on all sales above $50,000.00.
prompt: Answer ALL parts of the question, showing your working. (This question is the Consumer Arithmetic and Computation question of Section I and carries 10 marks.)

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the cash price of the refrigerator.
markScheme: 1 mark for finding the discount, $720.00.
1 mark for the cash price, $4,080.00.
Award the answer mark for their own correct subtraction even if the discount is wrong.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the total hire-purchase price and the extra amount paid compared with the cash price.
markScheme: 1 mark for the deposit, $960.00.
1 mark for the total hire-purchase price, $5,424.00.
1 mark for the extra amount, $1,344.00.
Follow through their cash price from (a) for the extra amount.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: A customer invests $8,000.00 at 6% per annum compound interest for 2 years. Calculate the total interest earned.
markScheme: 1 mark for using the compound-interest formula with n = 2.
1 mark for the amount, $8,988.80 (or 1 mark for 8,000.00 x 1.06 = 8,480.00 as a first step).
1 mark for the interest, $988.80.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: A sales assistant sells $78,000.00 worth of goods in March. Calculate her total earnings for the month.
markScheme: 1 mark for the commission, $560.00 (commission is paid only on sales ABOVE $50,000.00).
1 mark for total earnings, $2,960.00.

planningHints: Deal with each part separately and label your answers (a), (b), (c), (d).
Percentages can be found with a decimal multiplier: 15% off means multiply by 0.85.
examinerTips: In (b) read the question again at the end: it asks for the total AND the extra amount.

title: Measurement: the school garden
source:
A school is laying out a rectangular garden measuring 12 m by 8 m.

Inside the garden there is a circular fish pond of diameter 4 m.

The rest of the garden is to be sown with grass seed, which is sold in boxes. Each box covers 10 m2 and costs $18.50.

A fence is to be erected around the whole garden, leaving a gate opening of 1.2 m. (Take pi = 3.14.)
prompt: Answer ALL parts of the question, showing your working. (This question is the Measurement question of Section I and carries 10 marks.)

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the area of the garden.
parts.modelAnswer: Area = length x width = 12 x 8 = 96 m2.
markScheme: 1 mark for 96 m2.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the area of the pond.
markScheme: 1 mark for the radius, 2 m.
1 mark for using pi r^2 to get 12.56 m2 (accept 12.56).

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Calculate the area that will be sown with grass seed.
markScheme: 1 mark for 83.44 m2 (follow through an incorrect pond area).
Accept 83.44 m2.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Determine the LEAST number of boxes of seed that must be bought, and the cost of the seed.
parts.modelAnswer:
Boxes needed = 83.44 / 10 = 8.344, so 9 whole boxes must be bought (you cannot buy part of a box).
Cost = 9 x $18.50 = $166.50.
markScheme: 1 mark for dividing the grass area by 10 to get about 8.344 boxes.
1 mark for rounding UP to 9 boxes and saying why.
1 mark for the cost, $166.50.
No mark for 8 boxes: part boxes cannot be bought.

parts.label: (e)
parts.prompt: Calculate the length of fencing needed for the garden.
parts.modelAnswer:
Perimeter = 2(l + w) = 2(12 + 8) = 40 m.
Fencing = 40 - 1.2 = 38.8 m.
markScheme: 1 mark for the perimeter, 40 m.
1 mark for subtracting the 1.2 m gate.
1 mark for the answer 38.8 m.

planningHints: Sketch the garden and write the measurements on it before you start.
In (d) think about what is physically possible, not just the arithmetic.
examinerTips: Rounding up in (d) is worth a mark of its own: the reason must appear in your answer.

title: Statistics: goals scored in a season
source:
A football team played 20 matches in a season, and the number of goals scored in each match was recorded:

  0 goals: 2 matches
  1 goals: 5 matches
  2 goals: 6 matches
  3 goals: 4 matches
  4 goals: 2 matches
  5 goals: 1 matches

Total matches: 20. Total goals scored: 42.
prompt: Answer ALL parts of the question. (This question is the Statistics question of Section I and carries 10 marks.)

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: State the mode of the number of goals scored.
parts.modelAnswer: The mode is 2 goals, because 2 goals were scored in 6 matches, more often than any other number.
markScheme: 1 mark for 2 (with or without a reason).

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the mean number of goals scored per match.
parts.modelAnswer: Mean = total goals / number of matches = 42 / 20 = 2.10 goals per match.
markScheme: 1 mark for using total goals / number of matches.
1 mark for the total, 42 goals (from the frequency table).
1 mark for 2.10.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find the median number of goals scored.
parts.modelAnswer: With 20 matches the median is the mean of the 10th and 11th values when the results are put in order. Both fall in the group of 6 matches with 2 goals, so the median is 2 goals.
markScheme: 1 mark for ordering the 20 results (or for finding the 10th and 11th values).
1 mark for the median, 2 (accept 2.0).

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: In the next match the team scores 7 goals. State, with a reason, how this affects the mean number of goals per match.
parts.modelAnswer: The new mean is (42 + 7) / 21 = 2.33 goals, so the mean increases from 2.10 to 2.33. The mean rises because 7 is greater than the old mean.
markScheme: 1 mark for the new mean, 2.33.
1 mark for stating that the mean increases, with the reason that 7 exceeds the previous mean.

parts.label: (e)
parts.prompt: A match is selected at random from the 20 matches. Find the probability that exactly 2 goals were scored in it.
markScheme: 1 mark for the fraction 6/20.
1 mark for the answer 0.3 or 3/10 in its simplest form.

planningHints: A frequency table is a quick way to record the numbers before you calculate.
Show the working for the total: 0x2 + 1x5 + 2x6 + ...
examinerTips: In (d) 'state ... with a reason' means both the effect and why.

title: Algebra: simultaneous equations, quadratics and inequalities
source:
A small business makes and sells x items a week. Its income is modelled by the straight-line graph y = 3x - 5 and its costs are modelled by the line y = 11 - x, where y is in hundreds of dollars. The business breaks even when its income equals its costs.

Its profit for a different product is modelled by the quadratic expression x2 - 7x + 12 (in hundreds of dollars) for x thousand items sold, and it is preparing a rectangular sign whose length is (x + 3) cm and width (x - 1) cm.
prompt: Answer ALL parts of the question, showing your working. (This question is the Algebra question of Section I and carries 15 marks.)

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Solve the pair of simultaneous equations y = 3x - 5 and y = 11 - x.
parts.modelAnswer:
3x - 5 = 11 - x
3x + x = 11 + 5
4x = 16
x = 4
y = 3(4) - 5 = 7
Check with the second equation: 11 - 4 = 7, so the solution is x = 4, y = 7.
markScheme: 1 mark for equating the two expressions (3x - 5 = 11 - x).
1 mark for collecting terms to get 4x = 16.
1 mark for x = 4.
1 mark for y = 7 (or for checking the second equation).

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Factorise x2 - 7x + 12 and hence solve x2 - 7x + 12 = 0.
markScheme: 1 mark for (x - 3)(x - 4) (or for two correct factors).
1 mark for x = 3.
1 mark for x = 4.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Solve the inequality 5x - 3 < 2x + 9 and show the solution on a number line.
parts.modelAnswer:
5x - 3 < 2x + 9
5x - 2x < 9 + 3
3x < 12
x < 4
On a number line, draw an open circle at 4 and shade the arrow pointing to the left.
markScheme: 1 mark for 3x < 12.
1 mark for x < 4.
1 mark for a correct number line: open (unshaded) circle at 4, arrow to the left.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: The rectangular sign has length (x + 3) cm and width (x - 1) cm, and its area is 45 cm2. Form an equation in x, solve it, and state the dimensions of the sign.
parts.modelAnswer:
(x + 3)(x - 1) = 45
x2 + 2x - 3 = 45
x2 + 2x - 48 = 0
(x + 8)(x - 6) = 0
x = -8 or x = 6.
A length cannot be negative, so x = 6.
Length = 6 + 3 = 9 cm, width = 6 - 1 = 5 cm.
Check: 9 x 5 = 45 cm2.
markScheme: 1 mark for forming (x + 3)(x - 1) = 45.
1 mark for expanding to x2 + 2x - 48 = 0.
1 mark for factorising to (x + 8)(x - 6) = 0.
1 mark for rejecting x = -8 with the reason that a length must be positive.
1 mark for 9 cm by 5 cm (or for checking 9 x 5 = 45).

planningHints: In (a) both expressions equal y, so they equal each other.
In (d) always test both roots against the context of the question.
examinerTips: Do not lose the context marks: a root that is mathematically correct can still be rejected with a reason, and that reason earns a mark.

title: Relations, functions and graphs: the line through A and B
source:
The points A(2, 1) and B(6, 5) lie on a straight line.

The function f is defined by f(x) = 2x2 - 3x + 1.
prompt: Answer ALL parts of the question, showing your working. (This question is the Relations, Functions and Graphs question of Section I and carries 10 marks.)

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the gradient of the line AB.
markScheme: 1 mark for substituting into (y2 - y1)/(x2 - x1).
1 mark for the gradient 1.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Determine the equation of the line AB in the form y = mx + c.
parts.modelAnswer:
m = 1, and A(2, 1) lies on the line, so 1 = 1(2) + c, giving c = -1.
The equation is y = x - 1.
markScheme: 1 mark for substituting a point into y = x + c to find c = -1.
1 mark for y = x - 1.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find the coordinates of the point where the line AB crosses the x-axis.
parts.modelAnswer: At the x-axis y = 0: 0 = x - 1, so x = 1. The line crosses the x-axis at (1, 0).
markScheme: 1 mark for putting y = 0 (or reading the intercept from a sketch).
1 mark for (1, 0).

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Find the coordinates of the midpoint of AB.
markScheme: 1 mark for adding the coordinates correctly.
1 mark for (4, 3).

parts.label: (e)
parts.prompt: Evaluate f(-2) for f(x) = 2x2 - 3x + 1.
markScheme: 1 mark for 2(4) - 3(-2) + 1 with the signs handled correctly.
1 mark for 15.
Common error: (-2)^2 = 4, not -4.

planningHints: A sketch of the two points helps you see whether the gradient should be positive.
For f(-2) write the substitution out in full before simplifying.
examinerTips: In (c) the x-axis means y = 0; in (e) watch the signs of a negative input.

title: Geometry and trigonometry: the flagpole, the circle and the cosine rule
source:
A vertical flagpole stands on level ground. A straight wire runs from the top of the pole to a point on the ground 9 m from the foot of the pole. The pole is 12 m tall.

In a different diagram, AB is a diameter of a circle with centre O and C is a point on the circumference. Angle ABC = 35 degrees.

In triangle XYZ, XY = 7 cm, XZ = 9 cm and angle YXZ = 60 degrees.

Finally, a ladder 5 m long rests against a vertical wall with its foot 2 m from the wall.
prompt: Answer ALL parts of the question, showing your working. (This question is the Geometry and Trigonometry question of Section I and carries 20 marks.)

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the length of the wire from the top of the flagpole to the point on the ground.
parts.modelAnswer:
The pole is vertical, so the wire, the pole and the ground form a right-angled triangle with the right angle at the foot of the pole.
Wire^2 = 12^2 + 9^2 = 144 + 81 = 225
Wire = sqrt(225) = 15 m.
markScheme: 1 mark for recognising a right-angled triangle and using Pythagoras' theorem.
1 mark for 15 m (accept 15 m).

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the angle of elevation of the top of the pole from the point on the ground.
parts.modelAnswer:
tan(theta) = opposite/adjacent = 12/9 = 1.3333
theta = tan^-1(1.3333) = 53.1 degrees (to the nearest 0.1 degree).
markScheme: 1 mark for choosing tan with opposite 12 and adjacent 9.
1 mark for 1.3333 or for tan^-1(4/3).
1 mark for 53.1 degrees (accept 53 degrees or 53.1 degrees).

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Explain why angle ACB is a right angle, and calculate the size of angle BAC.
parts.modelAnswer:
Angle ACB is the angle in a semicircle: AB is a diameter, so the angle subtended by AB at any point C on the circumference is 90 degrees.
In triangle ACB, the angles add to 180 degrees:
angle BAC = 180 - 90 - 35 = 55 degrees.
markScheme: 1-2 marks for the reason: the angle in a semicircle is a right angle (2 marks).
1 mark for using the angle sum of a triangle (180 degrees).
1 mark for 55 degrees.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: In triangle XYZ, calculate (i) the length YZ and (ii) the area of triangle XYZ.
parts.modelAnswer:
(i) Cosine rule: YZ^2 = XY^2 + XZ^2 - 2(XY)(XZ)cos(X)
= 7^2 + 9^2 - 2(7)(9)cos 60 degrees
= 49 + 81 - 63.0
= 67.0
YZ = sqrt(67.0) = 8.19 cm.

(ii) Area = 1/2 x XY x XZ x sin(X) = 0.5 x 7 x 9 x sin 60 degrees = 0.5 x 7 x 9 x 0.8660 = 27.28 cm2.
markScheme: 1 mark for the correct form of the cosine rule.
1 mark for substituting the three values correctly.
1 mark for YZ^2 = 67.0.
1 mark for YZ = 8.19 cm (accept 8.2 cm).
1 mark for the area formula 1/2 ab sin C.
1 mark for the area, 27.28 cm2 (accept 27.3 cm2).

parts.label: (e)
parts.prompt: Calculate the height the ladder reaches up the wall and the angle the ladder makes with the ground.
parts.modelAnswer:
Height^2 = 5^2 - 2^2 = 25 - 4 = 21, so height = sqrt(21) = 4.58 m.
cos(theta) = 2/5 = 0.4, so theta = 66.4 degrees.
markScheme: 1 mark for using Pythagoras to get the height, 4.58 m.
1 mark for using cos (adjacent/hypotenuse) for the angle with the ground.
1 mark for 66.4 degrees.

planningHints: Draw a separate, labelled diagram for each part of this question.
Write down which ratio you are using (sin, cos or tan) and why.
examinerTips: The angle of elevation is measured UP from the horizontal; name the sides of the triangle before you substitute into a ratio.

title: Combination question: the school water tank
source:
A school is installing a cylindrical water tank to store water during the dry season. The tank has a radius of 1.5 m and a height of 2 m.

The inside of the tank, including the base, must be painted with two coats to protect the water. One litre of paint covers 8 m2.

A pump fills the tank at 15 litres per minute. (Take pi = 3.14; 1 m3 = 1000 litres.)
prompt: Answer ALL parts of the question, showing your working. (This is the combination question/investigation of Section I and carries 10 marks. It combines Measurement, Computation and Number Theory.)

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the volume of the tank in cubic metres.
markScheme: 1 mark for using pi r^2 h with r = 1.5 and h = 2.
1 mark for 14.13 m3 (accept 14.1 m3).

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Determine how many litres of water the tank holds when full.
markScheme: 1 mark for 14,130.00 litres (accept 14 130 litres).

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Determine the least number of whole litres of paint that must be bought to give the inside of the tank two coats.
parts.modelAnswer:
Curved surface = 2 pi r h = 2 x 3.14 x 1.5 x 2 = 18.84 m2.
Base = pi r^2 = 3.14 x 2.25 = 7.07 m2.
One coat = 18.84 + 7.07 = 25.91 m2.
Two coats = 2 x 25.91 = 51.81 m2.
Paint = 51.81 / 8 = 6.48 litres, so 7 whole litres must be bought.
markScheme: 1 mark for the curved surface area, 18.84 m2.
1 mark for the base area, 7.07 m2.
1 mark for doubling to allow for two coats: 51.81 m2.
1 mark for rounding UP to 7 litres, with the reason that part litres cannot be bought.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: The pump is switched on at 08:00. Determine the time, to the nearest minute, at which the tank will be full.
parts.modelAnswer:
Time = 14,130.00 litres / 15 litres per minute = 942.0 minutes.
942.0 minutes = 15 hours and 42 minutes.
08:00 + 15 hours 42 minutes = 23:42.
markScheme: 1 mark for dividing the capacity by the flow rate to get 942.0 minutes.
1 mark for converting to 15 hours 42 minutes (not a decimal of an hour).
1 mark for 23:42 (accept 11:42 p.m.).

planningHints: Part (c) is an 'investigation': decide what surfaces are painted and how many coats.
In (d) convert minutes into hours AND minutes before adding to the start time.
examinerTips: Marks are given for the reasoning in (c) and (d), so state why you round up and how you converted the time.

title: Algebra and graphs: the height of a thrown ball
source:
A ball is thrown vertically upwards. Its height, h metres, above the ground after t seconds is given by h = 20t - 5t2.

A table of values is to be completed for t = 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4, and the graph of h against t drawn on graph paper.
prompt: Answer ALL parts of the question. (This is a Section II question carrying 15 marks; in the real Paper 02 you answer any TWO of the three Section II questions in about 20 minutes each.)

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Complete the table of values for t = 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4, showing your substitutions for t = 2.
markScheme: 1 mark for h = 20 at t = 2 with the substitution shown.
1 mark for all five values correct: 0, 15, 20, 15, 0.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Draw the graph of h against t for 0 <= t <= 4, using a scale of 2 cm for 1 second on the t-axis and 1 cm for 5 m on the h-axis.
parts.modelAnswer: Plot the points (0, 0), (1, 15), (2, 20), (3, 15) and (4, 0), then join them with a smooth curve. The curve is symmetrical about the line t = 2 and is highest at t = 2.
markScheme: 1 mark for plotting at least four points correctly.
1 mark for a smooth symmetrical curve (not straight lines between the points).
1 mark for correct labelling: axes named with units, a scale and a title.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: From your graph, state the maximum height reached by the ball and the time at which it occurs.
parts.modelAnswer: The maximum height is 20 m, reached at t = 2 seconds.
markScheme: 1 mark for 20 m.
1 mark for t = 2 seconds.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Solve 20t - 5t2 = 0 and explain what the two solutions mean in this problem.
parts.modelAnswer:
20t - 5t2 = 0
5t(4 - t) = 0
t = 0 or t = 4.
t = 0 is the moment the ball is thrown (on the ground); t = 4 is the moment it returns to the ground.
markScheme: 1 mark for factorising 5t(4 - t) = 0 (or an equivalent method).
1 mark for t = 0 and t = 4.
1 mark for explaining both: the ball leaves the ground at 0 s and lands 4 s later.

parts.label: (e)
parts.prompt: Use your graph to find the two times at which the ball is 15 m above the ground.
parts.modelAnswer: Drawing the line h = 15 m across the graph cuts the curve at t = 1 s and t = 3 s.
markScheme: 1 mark for t = 1 s.
1 mark for t = 3 s.

parts.label: (f)
parts.prompt: Show that the ball is 10 m above the ground when t2 - 4t + 2 = 0, and solve this equation, giving your answers to 2 decimal places.
parts.modelAnswer:
h = 10 gives 20t - 5t2 = 10.
Dividing by 5: 4t - t2 = 2, that is t2 - 4t + 2 = 0.
Using the formula: t = (4 +/- sqrt(16 - 8))/2 = (4 +/- sqrt(8))/2.
sqrt(8) = 2.83, so t = 0.59 or t = 3.41 (2 d.p.).
markScheme: 1 mark for forming t2 - 4t + 2 = 0 from 20t - 5t2 = 10.
1 mark for using the quadratic formula with a = 1, b = -4, c = 2.
1 mark for t = 0.59 and t = 3.41 (2 d.p.).

planningHints: Complete the table first: every later part depends on the graph being right.
Use a sharp pencil and label the curve; a sketch without a scale loses marks.
examinerTips: In (f) 'show that' means the working must lead to the printed equation - a bare answer earns nothing.

title: Measurement and geometry: painting the shed and the diagonal brace
source:
A school workshop is a rectangular shed 4 m long, 3 m wide and 2.5 m high.

The walls and the ceiling are to be painted white. The shed has one door 1 m by 2 m and two windows, each 1 m by 1 m, which are not painted.

Paint is sold in tins covering 6 m2 each and costing $18.75 a tin.

A metal brace is to run from a floor corner of the shed to the opposite ceiling corner.
prompt: Answer ALL parts of the question, showing your working. (This is a Section II question carrying 15 marks; in the real Paper 02 you answer any TWO of the three Section II questions.)

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the total area of the four walls.
parts.modelAnswer:
Two long walls: 2 x (4 x 2.5) = 20.0 m2.
Two end walls: 2 x (3 x 2.5) = 15.0 m2.
Total wall area = 20.0 + 15.0 = 35.0 m2.
markScheme: 1 mark for the area of one long wall, 10.0 m2.
1 mark for the area of one end wall, 7.5 m2.
1 mark for doubling both pairs.
1 mark for the total, 35.0 m2.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the area of the ceiling and the total area of the door and windows.
parts.modelAnswer:
Ceiling = 4 x 3 = 12.0 m2.
Door and windows = (1 x 2) + 2(1 x 1) = 2 + 2 = 4 m2.
markScheme: 1 mark for the ceiling, 12.0 m2.
1 mark for the door area, 2 m2.
1 mark for the two windows, 2 m2 (total 4 m2).

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Calculate the area to be painted.
markScheme: 1 mark for adding the walls and ceiling, 47.0 m2.
1 mark for subtracting the door and windows to get 43.0 m2.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Determine the least number of tins of paint needed and the total cost of the paint.
parts.modelAnswer:
Tins = 43.0 / 6 = 7.17, so 8 tins must be bought.
Cost = 8 x $18.75 = $150.00.
markScheme: 1 mark for dividing the painted area by 6 m2.
1 mark for rounding UP to 8 tins with a reason.
1 mark for the cost, $150.00.

parts.label: (e)
parts.prompt: Calculate the length of the metal brace, giving your answer to 2 decimal places.
parts.modelAnswer:
The brace is the space diagonal:
brace^2 = 4^2 + 3^2 + 2.5^2 = 16.0 + 9.0 + 6.25 = 31.25
brace = sqrt(31.25) = 5.59 m.
markScheme: 1 mark for squaring all three dimensions.
1 mark for adding the three squares to get 31.25.
1 mark for 5.59 m (2 d.p.).

planningHints: Draw the shed as a net or a labelled sketch before you calculate.
Diagonal questions in three dimensions are solved by applying Pythagoras twice.
examinerTips: Only the two decimal places asked for in (e) are required - do not lose time writing extra figures.

title: Vectors and matrices: position vectors and a matrix solution
source:
In a coordinate system, the position vectors a and b are given by a = (3, 4) and b = (-1, 2) written as column vectors.

The points A(1, 2), B(3, 6) and C(5, 10) are also marked on the same grid.

The matrix M = (2 1 / 3 4) is used to solve the simultaneous equations 2x + y = 10 and 3x + 4y = 25.
prompt: Answer ALL parts of the question, showing your working. (This is a Section II question carrying 15 marks; in the real Paper 02 you answer any TWO of the three Section II questions.)

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate a + 2b as a column vector.
markScheme: 1 mark for 2b = (-2, 4).
1 mark for (1, 8).

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of a, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.
markScheme: 1 mark for sqrt(3^2 + 4^2).
1 mark for 5 (5.00 to 3 s.f.).

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Show that the points A(1, 2), B(3, 6) and C(5, 10) are collinear.
parts.modelAnswer:
AB = (3 - 1, 6 - 2) = (2, 4).
BC = (5 - 3, 10 - 6) = (2, 4).
AB = BC, so AB and BC are parallel; because they share the point B, the three points lie on one straight line. (AB = BC also shows B is the midpoint of AC.)
markScheme: 1 mark for AB = (2, 4).
1 mark for BC = (2, 4) and the statement that the vectors are equal (parallel).
1 mark for the reason: because they share B, the points are collinear.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: For M = (2 1 / 3 4), calculate the determinant of M and write down M inverse.
markScheme: 1 mark for the determinant, 5.
1 mark for interchanging 2 and 4 on the leading diagonal.
1 mark for changing the signs of the other two elements (-1 and -3).
1 mark for the complete inverse, 1/5 x (4 -1 / -3 2).

parts.label: (e)
parts.prompt: Use M and M inverse to solve 2x + y = 10 and 3x + 4y = 25.
markScheme: 1 mark for writing the equations in matrix form.
1 mark for multiplying M^-1 by the column vector (10 / 25).
1 mark for (15 / 20) divided by 5.
1 mark for x = 3 and y = 4.

planningHints: Write column vectors in the correct order - top element is the x-component.
Show the matrix multiplication one row at a time so the method is visible.
examinerTips: In (c) the words 'because they share the point B' carry a mark: equal vectors alone do not prove collinearity.
